title: When Row-Rectangular Relaxations Preserve Sharp Terminal Causal Contrasts in Shared-Root Serial SCMs
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < field threshold 7.4; direct growing-horizon complexity remains open and extended-law hardness lacks a demonstrated econometric application.
gap_reasons: The note proves coNP-completeness only for the high-dimensional extended root-law encoding, already at one stage; for both direct encodings it proves coNP membership and an L^{O(H)} XP algorithm but leaves the exact growing-horizon complexity open.

The extended hardness result also derives its force from arbitrary bounded lift coordinates encoded through duplicated response types, without an application demonstrating that such compact extended laws arise in econometric practice.
proof_attempt_summary: The run classified universal terminal-law equality for shared versus row-rectangular two-world SCM transitions. It discharged coNP membership for all three encodings, coNP-hardness for extended descriptions at one stage, and an L^{O(H)} XP algorithm for the two direct encodings, but could not settle their growing-horizon complexity. The mathematics passed both rubric and math review; the result was downgraded because the open direct branch and the absence of a natural econometric extended-law application cap its significance below the field floor.
tldr: When may a tractable row-rectangular relaxation replace a shared-root binary serial SCM without changing any sharp terminal causal contrast? The representation-sensitive classification compares \(C_Q\) and \(C_R\) through exact fixed-reward support-path verifiers for explicit vertices, direct sixteen-mass inequalities, and extended root laws. Polynomial-bit separation gives coNP membership for all three encodings, while the audited one-stage causal reduction gives coNP-completeness for extended descriptions. The two direct encodings are polynomially equivalent and admit a representation-preserving \(L^{O(H)}\) algorithm, so they are in XP parameterized by the explicit horizon and are polynomial-time decidable for every fixed horizon bound. Their exact growing-horizon complexity remains open: polynomial time, coNP-completeness through coNP-hardness, and intermediate complexity are all left available. Bellman-cone compression and horizon-carried causal hardness are candidate approaches, not an exhaustive dichotomy.
gap: Rectangular robust-MDP theory explains why independent row choices admit Bellman recursion, and response-function SCM work explains why categorical counterfactual models form projected mass polytopes. Neither literature classifies equality between the shared-law and row-rectangular terminal bodies for a fixed initial two-world law, four pair states, sixteen deterministic response types, and an explicit serial horizon. Generic containment hardness does not preserve those restrictions.
fill: Establish the fixed-reward verifier as three encoding-specific supporting theorems, use it rather than a black box in the separator-to-coNP proof, retain the one-stage extended lower bound only after every planar, homogenization, transport, and probability-substitution map passes, and then settle the remaining growing-horizon direct case by either compressing variable-reward Bellman-cone coverage or constructing horizon-carried causal hardness.
